_comment: How a spoken turn says it is one (T-0644). `prompt.submit` carries `params.voice: true` from every spoken turn, whatever the speaker gate said; aura-adapter/aura_adapter/effort.py reads it (or a speaker_ticket) to run the turn at VOICE_REASONING_EFFORT, and speaker.py strips it before Hermes. The ticket keeps its meaning (WHO spoke, only when the gate accepted the voice); `voice` is HOW the words arrived, so a voice the gate refused, or a gate that is off, still gets the voice effort. A typed turn (the dock's text box, a slash command's `send`, a routine, the car's drive start and message announcements) never sends the key: it is omitted, not false. Readers: aura-adapter/tests/test_effort.py (the adapter), aura-web/src/lib/hud/voice.flag.test.ts (the console mic, which the car's /car page and the phone's ConsolePage run), android-app/tools/voice_flag_test.py (the phone's own conversation and the car's native voice path). The `senders` below are the files and the exact text each must contain; a sender that stops sending it fails the suite that owns its file.

console_mic.needle: await this.submit(String(body.transcript), body.speaker_ticket ?? null, null, true);

car_page.note: the /car page is the console in a web view: it speaks through console_mic and console_link, no Kotlin of its own
